data.current_description: Seven-level cascading query for make/model/year dropdowns. type=car (default) or type=motorcycle selects the cascade; IDs are the same kind in both. Call with no parameters to list makes, then add make, model, year, series, engine and variant one at a time; the last level returns a list of vehicle records, each with a vehicle_id (usually one; fewer than 100 paths return two vehicles whose catalogue entries overlap in that year). Pass every value exactly as returned by the previous level and URL-encode it: values contain commas, double spaces, braces, brackets and slashes, and matching is exact including letter case, so make=toyota or a collapsed double space returns an empty list. An empty-string series is a real value; send series= (empty) to continue. Unknown values return 200 with an empty data list, not an error. vehicle_id is a stable ID for the variant (the same for every model year it was sold) and is the same ID /api/v1/lookup returns. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward the monthly lookup quota. 500 requests/minute rate limit. Keep the API key on your server, not in browser JavaScript.
data.summary_suggestion: Browse vehicle database by make, model, and year
data.description_suggestion: Cascading query interface to browse the vehicle database by make, model, year, series, engine, and variant. Start with no parameters to list available makes, then progressively add parameters to narrow results. Returns vehicle_id values that can be used with /api/v1/vehicles/{vehicle_id} or /api/v1/lookup. Requires Starter-or-above API key. Does not consume monthly lookup quota. Supports both cars (default) and motorcycles. Values are case-sensitive and must be URL-encoded; pass values exactly as returned by previous queries.

Description is overly technical with implementation details (null fields, example IDs) that obscure the primary purpose. data.current_description: Returns the vehicle database record for one vehicle_id, as returned by /api/v1/lookup (on vehicle and on each alternatives entry, null when not certain) and by the last level of /api/v1/vehicles. The ID identifies the variant, not the year, and is stable. detail is "full" for a complete record or "basic" (series, variant and long_description null, years empty) when only the ID and summary fields exist; e.g. 7295503 is a basic record and 1380801 (sandbox plate TEST123) is a full one. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward monthly lookup quota. Shares the 500 requests/minute vehicle database rate limit. If the requested ID has been merged into another (the database occasionally held one vehicle under two IDs), the response is the current record; compare its vehicle_id with the one requested.
data.summary_suggestion: Retrieve full vehicle record by ID
data.description_suggestion: Returns the complete vehicle database record for a given vehicle_id, including make, model, year range, series, variant, and engine details. Records may be returned in 'full' detail (complete information) or 'basic' detail (summary only). Vehicle IDs are stable identifiers for variants across model years. If a requested ID has been merged into another, the response returns the current record. Requires Starter-or-above API key. Does not consume monthly lookup quota.

data.current_summary: Vehicles added, updated or merged since a date
data.current_description: Lists the vehicles added, updated or merged since `since`, oldest change first, each as its vehicle_id with a slim summary (type, make, model, year range, detail, new model years). Use it to keep stored vehicle IDs or records current (for example products mapped to vehicles) without walking the cascade again: filter on make and model, fetch the full records you need from /api/v1/vehicles/{vehicle_id}, store `until` and pass it as `since` next time; while `has_more` is true, call again with `cursor=next_cursor`. Changes are reported from 2026-10-20 onwards and for the last 90 days. Cars and motorcycles are separate feeds (`type`). A vehicle first seen on a plate lookup appears as added with detail basic, then as updated when its full record arrives. Vehicle IDs are never deleted. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward monthly lookup quota. Shares the 500 requests/minute vehicle database rate limit.
data.description_suggestion: Lists vehicles added, updated, or merged in the vehicle database since a specified date, ordered oldest-first. Each entry includes vehicle_id, type (car/motorcycle), make, model, year range, and detail level. Supports cursor-based pagination for large result sets. Use this to keep cached vehicle records current without re-querying the full cascade. Changes are available for the last 90 days. Requires Starter-or-above API key. Does not consume monthly lookup quota.

data.current_description: Seven-level cascading query for make/model/year dropdowns. type=car (default) or type=motorcycle selects the cascade; IDs are the same kind in both. Call with no parameters to list makes, then add make, model, year, series, engine and variant one at a time; the last level returns a list of vehicle records, each with a vehicle_id (usually one; fewer than 100 paths return two vehicles whose catalogue entries overlap in that year). Pass every value exactly as returned by the previous level and URL-encode it: values contain commas, double spaces, braces, brackets and slashes, and matching is exact including letter case, so make=toyota or a collapsed double space returns an empty list. An empty-string series is a real value; send series= (empty) to continue. Unknown values return 200 with an empty data list, not an error. vehicle_id is a stable ID for the variant (the same for every model year it was sold) and is the same ID /api/v1/lookup returns. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward the monthly lookup quota. 500 requests/minute rate limit. Keep the API key on your server, not in browser JavaScript.

data.description_suggestion: Cascading query interface to browse the vehicle database by make, model, year, series, engine, and variant. Start with no parameters to list available makes, then progressively add parameters to narrow results. Returns vehicle_id values that can be used with /api/v1/vehicles/{vehicle_id} or /api/v1/lookup. Requires Starter-or-above API key. Does not consume monthly lookup quota. Supports both cars (default) and motorcycles. Values are case-sensitive and must be URL-encoded; pass values exactly as returned by previous queries.

data.current_description: Returns the vehicle database record for one vehicle_id, as returned by /api/v1/lookup (on vehicle and on each alternatives entry, null when not certain) and by the last level of /api/v1/vehicles. The ID identifies the variant, not the year, and is stable. detail is "full" for a complete record or "basic" (series, variant and long_description null, years empty) when only the ID and summary fields exist; e.g. 7295503 is a basic record and 1380801 (sandbox plate TEST123) is a full one. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward monthly lookup quota. Shares the 500 requests/minute vehicle database rate limit. If the requested ID has been merged into another (the database occasionally held one vehicle under two IDs), the response is the current record; compare its vehicle_id with the one requested.

data.current_summary: Vehicles added, updated or merged since a date
data.current_description: Lists the vehicles added, updated or merged since `since`, oldest change first, each as its vehicle_id with a slim summary (type, make, model, year range, detail, new model years). Use it to keep stored vehicle IDs or records current (for example products mapped to vehicles) without walking the cascade again: filter on make and model, fetch the full records you need from /api/v1/vehicles/{vehicle_id}, store `until` and pass it as `since` next time; while `has_more` is true, call again with `cursor=next_cursor`. Changes are reported from 2026-10-20 onwards and for the last 90 days. Cars and motorcycles are separate feeds (`type`). A vehicle first seen on a plate lookup appears as added with detail basic, then as updated when its full record arrives. Vehicle IDs are never deleted. Requires a Starter-or-above API key (Free and Lite get 403). Does not count toward monthly lookup quota. Shares the 500 requests/minute vehicle database rate limit.
data.description_suggestion: Lists vehicles added, updated, or merged in the vehicle database since a specified date, ordered oldest-first. Each entry includes vehicle_id, type (car/motorcycle), make, model, year range, and detail level. Use this to keep cached vehicle records current without re-querying the full cascade. Supports cursor-based pagination; store the `until` timestamp and pass it as `since` in the next request. Changes are available for the last 90 days. Requires Starter-or-above API key. Does not consume monthly lookup quota.
